title: Amplifiers, megaphone, props and carrying instruments on the bus
summary: No amplifiers early on, only a megaphone and later one crystal mic for the singer; no sets for bands; trunks rode on top of the bus and instruments inside racks.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Did they have amplifiers there? No amplifiers. Did you ever use an amplifier? Yeah.

Only time, not that I can remember in the early days, we used a megaphone like we used to use for the singer. And all of this high-powered mechanism they have now, no, we didn't have anything like that. So that came in later? Later, yes. After your band broke up? Well, possibly maybe just before we used the old crystal mics. One stand, one crystal mic. Mostly for the singer. Oh. Yeah.

What about the... When you were in a theater, would there have any sort of special sets in those days? The drops, you mean the props? Yeah, the drops and all that. Not necessarily. Not for a band? No, not for a band. No, not for a band. How would you carry the instruments and the trunk with the music? Where would they be carrying in the bus?

Oh, we had a top on the bus and we also had the, on the inside, we had racks on the inside. But we used the top part for the trunks, the clothing and the inside for the instruments. And we were talking about that, how dangerous it could be. Yes, it was. In those days you didn't realize that. Good break there. Why sure. Good break things. Very easy.
